subject: language_arts

unit.title: Spelling with suffixes
unit.essentialQuestion: How do I add an ending to a word so it's still spelled correctly?

title: Suffix sort (which rule?) — retrieval
objectives: By the end, I can choose the right suffix rule for any root word.

vocabulary.definition: the main word before any ending
a little ending (tail) added to a word
stick the suffix straight on — nothing changes
cross off the silent e before a vowel suffix
twin the last letter of a short-vowel word
change the final y to i (but keep y before -ing)

emphasize: This is RETRIEVAL — the child decides WHICH rule each word needs, then applies it.
The thinking routine: look at the END of the root → choose the rule → spell it.
Catch the cross-rule confusions: hope (drop-e) vs hop (double); play (just-add — vowel before the y) vs cry (y → i).

keyConcepts: the three sorting questions: silent e? short vowel + one consonant? ends in y?
applying the chosen rule to spell the suffixed form
the default: none of those → just add
misconceptions: hope/hop mix-ups (dropping when you should double and vice versa)
adding a rule where none applies: jump → 'jumpping', play → 'plaiing' (play just adds — vowel before the y)
sorting correctly but forgetting to apply the rule when spelling
hooks: The Spelling Sorting Office — every word must go in the right rule-bag, and a mis-filed word comes out spelled wrong!

plan.goal: Set up the Sorting Office game and retrieve the names of all four rules.
plan.note: Pure retrieval energy — the child should feel like an expert being handed a job, not a student being tested.
plan.successCriteria: Child names (or recognises) all four rules: just add, drop the e, double, y → i.

script.say: Welcome to the Spelling Sorting Office! Every word that arrives has to go in the right rule-bag: Just add, Drop the e, Double, or y to i. You're the sorting-office worker — your job is to read the end of each word and pop it in the correct bag. Mis-file one and the spelling goes wrong! Ready to sort? Quick recall first — name me the four rules we've learned.
script.adaptHints: Listen for all four rule names. If shaky, point to each column heading and give one example word: jump, hope, run, happy.

stuckProtocol: If the rule names are shaky: show the table with one example per column and re-ask — 'which rule is jump using?'

plan.goal: Model the three-question sorting routine and think aloud through bake, sit, cry, play.
plan.note: The routine is the lesson: END of the root → choose → spell. Think aloud slowly on bake; speed up by play.
plan.successCriteria: Child can recite the three questions in order.

script.say: Here's how I sort. I look at the END of the root and ask three quick questions. One — does it end in a silent e? Then DROP the e (hope). Two — is it a short vowel and one consonant, like run? Then DOUBLE. Three — does it end in y? Then y to i. If none of those, it just goes in JUST ADD (jump, play). Watch me sort bake: ends in silent e → Drop the e bag → baking.
script.adaptHints: Think aloud through sit (double → sitting), cry (y→i → cried) and play (just add — the y has a vowel before it → playing). Say 'Look at the END of the word — that tells you the rule' every time.

blocks.title: The Sorting Office's 3 questions
steps: 1. Silent e on the end? → DROP the e (hope → hoping)
2. One short vowel + one consonant? → DOUBLE (run → running)
3. Ends in y? → change y → i (happy → happier) — but keep y before -ing!
None of those? → JUST ADD (jump → jumping, play → playing)

plan.goal: Guided sort of the sneaky pairs: hope vs hop, happy vs play — the child sorts, the tutor probes the reasoning.
plan.note: hope/hop is THE contrast of the unit. Draw out the silent-e-vs-no-e difference explicitly.
plan.successCriteria: Child sorts hope → drop-e and hop → double, and explains the difference.

script.say: Sort these with me. Hope — what's on the end? So which bag? Now spell hope plus -ing. Next, hop — careful, this one's sneaky! What's different about it? … And two more: happy… and play. Watch out — play ends in y but it has a vowel just before it, so the y is happy where it is: just add!
script.adaptHints: For each card, ask 'what's on the END?' before allowing a sort. If hope/hop confuses, write both and circle the e.

blocks.prompt: Sort each word into its rule-bag.

wrongAnswers.why: mis-sorted; no e to drop and didn't double
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is there a silent e on run? No. Is it a short vowel and one consonant? Yes → which bag?

wrongAnswers.why: missed the short-vowel + one-consonant pattern
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read runing back — roo-ning? The u went long! What protects it?

plan.goal: The key diagnostic: run + -ing — the child must name the rule AND produce the spelling.
plan.note: Probe HOW they knew (what's on the end of run). Naming the reasoning is the retrieval win.
plan.successCriteria: Child answers 'double the consonant → running' and explains via the word's ending.

script.say: Which rule does run need to add -ing, and what do you get?
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'How did you know — what's on the end of run?' Listen for: one short vowel + one consonant.

blocks.explain: Run ends in one short vowel + one consonant → double the n: running.

check.question: Which rule does run need to add -ing, and what do you get?

wrongAnswers.why: mis-sorted; no e to drop and didn't double
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is there a silent e on run? No. Is it a short vowel and one consonant? Yes → double. Move the card to the right bag.

wrongAnswers.why: cross-rule confusion
wrongAnswers.remedy: Re-read the end of the word and walk the three questions in order: silent e? short vowel + one consonant? ends in y?

plan.goal: Independent sorting and spelling: the full eight-card sort (jump, hope, run, happy, bake, sit, play, cry) plus interleaved spell-its from the bank.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2 — the full sort (l09-p04) is the centrepiece; surround it with spell-it items so sorting always ends in spelling.
plan.successCriteria: Child sorts at least six of eight words correctly and spells the suffixed forms accurately (esp. hoping/hopping).

script.say: The morning post has arrived, sorting-office worker — eight words, four bags! Sort each one, then spell it with -ing or -ed to prove the bag was right. Read the end of the word before you file it!
script.adaptHints: Frame the 'post' with the child's interests (parcels of dinosaurs, football stickers). The words themselves never change.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'let's check the end of this word again.'
Step down: narrow to three columns or pre-group the cards roughly.
ONE hint: ask just one of the three questions ('does it end in a silent e?').
Re-ask a smaller version (sort two cards only), then build back up.
Keep it safe: 'Sorting takes a careful eye — read the end and we'll check together.'

plan.goal: Child recites the three sorting questions; end on process praise for expert sorting.
plan.note: Child-led. This routine feeds the End-of-Unit 2 check (spell hopping, hoped, happier).
plan.successCriteria: Child states: silent e? → drop; short vowel + one consonant? → double; ends in y? → y → i; else → just add.

script.say: You're a top sorting-office worker. Tell me the three questions you ask to choose the right bag. … That's it. You read the end of every word and chose the right rule — even the sneaky hope-and-hop pair. That's careful, expert spelling.
script.adaptHints: If a question is missed, point at the steps list and let the child fill the gap themselves.

blocks.prompt: Say the three sorting questions out loud, like you're training a new sorting-office worker.
blocks.target: Silent e? Drop it. Short vowel and one consonant? Double it. Ends in y? Change y to i. Otherwise — just add!

block.prompt: Two bags only: sort these words.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: jump/play → Just add; bake/smile → Drop the e

wrongAnswers.why: saw a letter to remove where there is none
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does play end in a silent e? Look at the last letter — what is it?

wrongAnswers.why: missed the silent e
wrongAnswers.remedy: Say bake — hear the long a? That's the silent e's magic. What must it do before -ing?

hints: Question 1 only: silent e on the end?
jump and play have no silent e.

reteach.say: Easy sort, one question: silent e on the end? Bake and smile — yes, e on the end → Drop bag. Jump and play — no e → Just add bag. One look at the last letter does it.

practiceBank.skill: name the rule for a word

block.prompt: Which bag does happy go in?
block.explain: Happy ends in y (with a consonant before it) → the y → i bag: happier, happiest.

wrongAnswers.why: didn't check the ending
wrongAnswers.remedy: Look at the last letter of happy. Which question does that trigger?

wrongAnswers.why: rule mix-up
wrongAnswers.remedy: Doubling is for short-vowel words like run. Happy ends in… what letter?

hints: Look at the LAST letter of happy.
Question 3: does it end in y?

reteach.say: Happy ends in y — that's question three! y → i bag: happy → happier. The end of the word always tells you the rule.

block.caption: happy ends in y → the y → i bag

block.prompt: Match each word to its rule.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: run→Double, hope→Drop the e, jump→Just add, cry→y → i

wrongAnswers.why: hope/hop confusion
wrongAnswers.remedy: Look at the end of hope — is there a silent e? Then which rule?

wrongAnswers.why: doubled where no doubling applies
wrongAnswers.remedy: Jump ends in TWO consonants (m, p) — not one. So no doubling needed. Which bag takes the leftovers?

hints: Walk the three questions for each word.
Only one of these words ends in a silent e.

reteach.say: Four words, four different endings: hope has the silent e (drop), run has short u + one n (double), cry ends in y (transform), and jump matches nothing — so it just adds. Every bag gets exactly one!

block.prompt: The full morning post! Sort all eight words into their rule-bags.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: jump/play → Just add; hope/bake → Drop the e; run/sit → Double; happy/cry → y → i

wrongAnswers.why: saw the y but missed the vowel before it
wrongAnswers.remedy: Play's y has a vowel (a) right before it — that y is comfy, it never changes. Which bag takes words that need no change?

wrongAnswers.why: hope/hop confusion
wrongAnswers.remedy: Spell hope out loud — h-o-p-e. There's the silent e! Which bag?

hints: Ask the three questions for every single word.
Each bag gets exactly two words.

reteach.say: Let's sort just the two sneakiest: hope has a silent e → Drop bag. Play ends in y BUT there's a vowel before it — that y never changes → Just add bag. Now try the other six with the three questions.

wrongAnswers.why: sorted into the Double bag — but hope has a silent e
wrongAnswers.remedy: Spell the root: h-o-p-e. See the e? Which bag — and what does the e do?

wrongAnswers.why: sorted correctly but didn't apply the rule
wrongAnswers.remedy: Right bag! Now DO the rule: the e hops off before -ing moves in.

hints: Question 1: silent e on the end of hope?
Cross the e, then add -ing.

reteach.say: Hope arrives at the office: silent e on the end → Drop bag → cross the e → hoping. One p, no e. (Hopping with twin p's belongs to hop!)

wrongAnswers.why: didn't double — that's hope's word (wishing)
wrongAnswers.remedy: Spell the root: h-o-p. No e! Short o, one p → which bag? What do twins protect?

wrongAnswers.why: invented a silent e
wrongAnswers.remedy: Hop has no e to drop. Short vowel + one consonant → double the p.

hints: Spell hop out loud — is there an e?
Short vowel + one consonant → twin letters.

reteach.say: Hop: h-o-p, short and bouncy, no e anywhere. Question two says YES — one short vowel, one consonant → double the p → hopping. The twin p's keep it bouncing.

block.caption: hop → hopping (twin p's, like twin bunnies)

wrongAnswers.why: sorted right but kept the y
wrongAnswers.remedy: Right bag — now do the transformation! Before -ed, the y becomes…?

wrongAnswers.why: grabbed the -ing exception form for an -ed build
wrongAnswers.remedy: Check the tail I asked for — it's -ed, not -ing. y → i, then -ed: cried.

hints: Cry ends in y — question three!
The suffix is -ed, so the y transforms.

reteach.say: Cry ends in y → y → i bag. The suffix is -ed (not -ing!), so the y transforms: cri + ed = cried. Only -ing would let the y stay: crying.

practiceBank.skill: read built words aloud across rules

block.prompt: Read the sorted post out loud: jumping… hoping… hopping… happier.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Reads all four words correctly, with hoping (long o) and hopping (short o) clearly different

wrongAnswers.answer: hoping and hopping read the same
wrongAnswers.why: not using the double letter as a sound clue
wrongAnswers.remedy: Look at the p's! One p — the o says its long name: HOH-ping. Twin p's — short and bouncy: HOP-ping.

wrongAnswers.why: read the root + suffix instead of the new word
wrongAnswers.remedy: The y already transformed — read the new word in two smooth beats: happi-er.

hints: Count the p's before you read.
Twin letters = short, bouncy sound.

reteach.say: Reading is the sorting-office's final check! One p in hoping — long o, a wishing word. Twin p's in hopping — short o, a bouncing word. Read each one and let the letters tell you the sound.

practiceBank.skill: spot the just-add trap (vowel before y)

wrongAnswers.why: applied y → i to a word where the y has a vowel before it
wrongAnswers.remedy: Look just before the y in play — there's an a! A y with a vowel friend never changes. Which bag?

wrongAnswers.why: doubled where no rule applies
wrongAnswers.remedy: Play matches none of the three questions — no silent e, not CVC, and its y has a vowel before it. So…just add!

hints: Check the letter BEFORE the y in play.
A y with a vowel before it stays put — just add.

reteach.say: The trickster of the office! Play ends in y, but peek before it — a vowel, a. A y with a vowel friend is comfy and never transforms. No silent e, no CVC pattern either… so play walks straight into Just add: playing.

practiceBank.skill: reject a rule where none applies

block.explain: Jump ends in TWO consonants (m, p) — no doubling needed. Just add: jumping.

wrongAnswers.why: added a rule where none applies — doubled after two consonants
wrongAnswers.remedy: Walk the questions: silent e? No. ONE short vowel + ONE consonant? Look — jump ends in m AND p, two consonants. So which bag?

hints: Count the consonants at the end of jump.
Doubling is only for ONE vowel + ONE consonant.

reteach.say: The doubling test is strict: exactly ONE vowel then ONE consonant. Jump ends in m-p — two consonants guarding the u already, no twins needed. Jump just adds: jumping. Extra rules make extra mistakes!

practiceBank.skill: explain a word that fits no bag neatly

block.prompt: The word 'see' arrives at the sorting office for -ing. Which bag does it go in — and why is it a bit tricky?
block.sample: Just add — seeing. It looks like it ends in e, but ee is a vowel team, not a silent e, so nothing is dropped.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Just add → seeing; the ee is a vowel team, not a silent e

wrongAnswers.why: treated the vowel-team ee like a silent e
wrongAnswers.remedy: Say see — do you HEAR that long e? A silent e is quiet; this e is doing the talking. Both e's stay: seeing.

wrongAnswers.why: guessed a rule instead of walking the questions
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is see a short-vowel word with one consonant at the end? It doesn't even end in a consonant! Which bag takes the words that match nothing?

hints: Say see out loud — is that e silent?
When a word matches none of the three questions, it just adds.

reteach.say: Expert-level post! See ends in ee — a LOUD vowel team, not a quiet silent e. It matches none of our three questions, so it takes the default bag: just add → seeing. The questions protect you even from brand-new words.

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level; at level 3, interleave sorting, spelling and explain-why items in a random order.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach, then narrow to a two-bag sort (level 1) before rebuilding to four bags.
adaptivity.masterySignal: 6+ of the 8 core words sorted correctly AND the suffixed forms spelled accurately (especially hoping/hopping) → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'choose the right suffix rule'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'let's check the end of this word again.'
Step down: narrow to three columns or pre-group the cards roughly.
ONE hint: ask just one of the three questions ('does it end in a silent e?').
Re-ask a smaller version (sort two cards only), then build back up.
Keep it safe: 'Sorting takes a careful eye — read the end and we'll check together.'
adaptivity.personalization: The 'post' can be parcels of anything the child loves (dinosaur cards, football stickers) and the office can be renamed after them — the root words themselves never change.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable sort; process praise: 'you read the end of every word before filing it — that's expert sorting.'

differentiation.support: Use three columns only (park y → i until secure) and pre-group the cards roughly so the child confirms rather than sorts from scratch.
differentiation.stretch: Add a 'trick' word that fits none of the four bags (see → seeing — a vowel team, not a silent e) and explain why.

extension: Invent two new word cards, sort them, and teach the rule back to the tutor.
assessmentEvidence: Child sorts at least six of eight words into the correct rule column and spells the suffixed forms accurately (esp. hoping/hopping).
revisitLater: Keep a couple of these cards for a warm-up before Lesson 10; this routine feeds the End-of-Unit 2 check (spell hopping, hoped, happier).
